name: frog
desc: A frog has no effective attacks. It feeds on small insects and typically dwells near water, in trees, or underground. The frog’s statistics can also be used to represent a toad.

special_abilities.name: amphibious
special_abilities.desc: The frog can breathe air and water

special_abilities.name: standing leap
special_abilities.desc: The frog's long jump is up to 10 ft. and its high jump is up to 5 ft., with or without a running start.

lore:
The common frog, though often overlooked by the novice traveler, is a master of the marshlands and shaded fens. These amphibians dwell where the veil between water and earth is thinnest, finding sanctuary in stagnant pools and the moss-slicked grottos of our world.

Though seemingly passive, the frog is a predator of startling precision. They are sit-and-wait hunters, camouflaged against the emerald muck until a victim draws near. With a lash of a prehensile, adhesive tongue—faster than a weary eye can blink—they snare their prey, dragging it into a maw that expands with unsettling elasticity to swallow the struggling catch whole.

In local lore, the frog is a creature of duality. To the peat-cutters of the Lowlands, their rhythmic chorus is a herald of coming storms, a collective prayer to the sky. Old wives’ tales suggest a frog upon one’s doorstep is a silent witness sent by the Hidden Folk to gather secrets. Some even whisper of "The Croaking King," a bog-spirit who demands a copper coin tossed into the reeds, lest he pull the unwary beneath the dark waters. Respect the silence of the pond, traveler.
